headline: GOLD HOLDS BELOW $4,350 AS FOMC CLOCK STARTS — 86% RATE-HIKE PROBABILITY NOW PRICED FOR SEPT 16
snippet: Gold trades at $4,348.90 as the Federal Reserve's two-day FOMC meeting begins September 15. CME FedWatch shows 86% probability of a 25bp rate hike — up from roughly 70% before August CPI — with Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference scheduled for September 16 at 2:30pm ET. Silver sits at $64.50. The Bank of Japan also meets September 17-18 where a further hike is expected, creating a dual central bank binary week for metals investors.

headline: GOLD REPATRIATION TREND HITS CONGRESS: U.S. HOLDS 8,133 TONNES FOR FOREIGN NATIONS — HOW LONG WILL THEY LEAVE IT THERE?
snippet: Foreign central banks have been accelerating repatriation requests from the New York Fed since 2025, with requests up approximately 40% year-over-year. The U.S. holds roughly 8,133 tonnes of gold in custody for foreign governments at Fort Knox and the New York Fed. Money Metals reports that several members of Congress are now questioning whether the arrangement remains viable as dollar credibility faces pressure from record fiscal deficits and shifting geopolitical alliances.

headline: KITCO WEEKLY SURVEY: WALL STREET TURNS FULLY BULLISH ON GOLD AHEAD OF FED — RETAIL HOLDS SLIM MAJORITY DESPITE 3 DOWN WEEKS
snippet: Kitco's September 11 weekly gold survey shows Wall Street analysts returning to a fully bullish consensus heading into FOMC week — reversing the mixed signals of the two prior weeks. Main Street retail investors hold a slim bullish majority despite three consecutive weekly losses. The divergence between institutional confidence and retail hesitation has historically signalled a contrarian entry point: institutions position ahead of binary catalysts while retail tends to lag the move.

headline: MONEY METALS: WHETHER FED HIKES OR HOLDS SEPT 16, THE GOLD THESIS DOESN'T CHANGE
snippet: A contrarian take published September 11 argues the FOMC rate decision is irrelevant to long-term precious metals investors. The structural drivers — U.S. fiscal deficits running at 6.8% of GDP, dollar reserve erosion, and central bank gold accumulation at 244 tonnes per quarter — are intact regardless of a 25bp hike or hold. The piece contends retail investors focused on Wednesday's binary event are missing the larger trend that has driven gold from $2,000 to $4,350 since 2022.

headline: GOLD $4,202–$4,510 RANGE THIS WEEK: TWO SCENARIOS MAPPED FOR THE FED BINARY — SILVER AT $64 IS THE LINE
snippet: Technical analysis for the week of September 15-21 frames gold's range at $4,202–$4,510 with the September 16 FOMC decision the sole catalyst. A 25bp hike with hawkish guidance risks a flush toward $4,200 support; a hold or dovish surprise could launch a breakout above $4,510 toward September highs. Silver at $64 is the key support level — if it holds through a hike scenario, it signals the structural bid is absorbing rate pressure and mining stocks should stabilize.

headline: RECORD $18B GOLD ETF INFLOWS IN AUGUST LIFT HOLDINGS TO ALL-TIME HIGH 4,189 TONNES — PHYSICAL BID HOLDS FLOOR AT $4,350
snippet: Despite August CPI lifting Fed rate-hike odds toward 90%, gold held $4,385 — a sign the institutional structural bid is absorbing paper-market rate pressure. World Gold Council data shows August gold ETF inflows hit $18 billion, the second-largest monthly total ever, lifting total holdings to a record 4,189 tonnes with AUM at $615 billion. European funds led with $7.9 billion in inflows, their strongest month on record, driven by UK and French institutional buying.

headline: AUSTRALIA'S MCA FIGHTS CGT DISCOUNT REMOVAL — 19% HIT TO JUNIOR EXPLORER INVESTOR RETURNS COULD DRY UP GREENFIELDS FUNDING
snippet: The Minerals Council of Australia (MCA) and Association of Mining and Exploration Companies (AMEC) are fighting proposed Treasury legislation that would remove the 50% CGT discount for investors in junior mineral explorers from July 2027, replacing it with inflation-indexed returns and a 30% minimum rate. The MCA calculates this cuts after-tax returns by 19% on a typical 5-year hold. With critical minerals exploration funding already competitive globally, both bodies warn the change could meaningfully reduce the capital available for greenfields discovery. Consultation closes September 28.

headline: ANGLO-TECK $54B MERGER AWAITS CHINA — SAMR CLEARANCE IS THE FINAL HURDLE, WINDOW CLOSES MARCH 2027
snippet: The proposed $54 billion Anglo American and Teck Resources merger into Anglo Teck plc has secured 99%+ shareholder approval and Canadian ICA clearance but is still awaiting Chinese SAMR and South Korean KFTC antitrust sign-off. Anglo American has flagged Chinese approval as the last substantive hurdle, with a completion window of September 2026 to March 2027. The merged entity would rank as a global top-3 copper producer and would hold the combined Teck copper and zinc assets alongside Anglo's existing portfolio.

headline: 38 NATIONS COMMIT TO TRIPLING NUCLEAR BY 2050 — URANIUM DEMAND COULD MORE THAN DOUBLE AS U3O8 SPOT HOLDS $90
snippet: Uranium prices hold near $90 per pound spot and $96.50 per pound for term contracts as utility demand accelerates globally. Thirty-eight countries representing over 70% of global GDP have backed a tripling of nuclear capacity by 2050. Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft each signed nuclear power agreements in 2026 for AI data centre load. The American Nuclear Society analysis estimates uranium demand could more than double within a decade if the tripling pledge is executed, putting sustained pressure on supply from Kazatomprom and Canada's Athabasca Basin operations.

headline: NW QUEENSLAND $3.4B EXPLORATION PUSH: SEISMIC AND GRAVITY SURVEYS UNLOCK NEW COPPER-CRITICAL MINERALS PROVINCE
snippet: Federal and Queensland governments are co-funding a $3.4 billion Resourcing Australia's Prosperity initiative targeting north-west Queensland's underexplored copper and critical minerals potential. A 840km Boodjamulla-Croydon reflection seismic survey is complete and an airborne gravity gradiometry survey is now underway north of Mount Isa. All data will be released to industry for exploration targeting. The region sits within the Cloncurry copper-gold district and is considered highly prospective for new polymetallic discoveries adjacent to existing infrastructure.

headline: LITHIUM SLIPS AS CHINA BATTERY FUTURES WEAKEN — AUSTRALIAN MINE RESTARTS ADD PRESSURE ON 2027 SUPPLY OUTLOOK
snippet: Lithium carbonate in China fell to 142,250 CNY/T on September 11, down further from the August maintenance-driven spike above 149,000. Battery futures are weakening on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange as Core Lithium's Finniss restart and Mineral Resources' Bald Hill resumption add to anticipated 2027 supply. Global lithium production is forecast to grow 26% year-over-year to 2.16 million tonnes in 2026 and 27% further in 2027, stoking fears of a structural surplus that would pressure prices for early-stage explorers seeking project financing.
